svg.title: Write down the two jobs — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Write down the two jobs
Your Windows host · Notepad lab notes
External practice user
Firewall / private lab boundary
RHEL 9 DMZ application server
NGINX · TLS ends here
Hosted practice application
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
Your notes list two different jobs, two private addresses and one application address.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. On your Windows PC, click Start, type Notepad, and open it. Save a new file as TLS lab notes.txt in
Documents.
2. Write: application server (TLS-APP01) = NGINX plus our small hosted practice page, 10.90.0.10/24.
3. Write: practice CA server (TLS-CA01) = a pretend signing office, 10.90.0.20/24. It is not a DoD CA.
4. Write: app.example.mil = the browser address for the practice application. It is a fictional example
used only by private hosts-file entries in this lab, not a domain you own.
5. Write: learner = the Linux user we will create on both new VMs. Keep passwords in your password
manager, not this notes file.
6. This course builds the TLS layer, not an enterprise firewall. The architecture diagram shows a real
edge-firewall pattern; our host-only network and RHEL firewalld model a private practice boundary. Never
publish these VMs.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
